name: Spotify
summary: Spotify describes its interviews on its careers site: a recruiter call, an interview with one or two team members, and a final round with several 'band members' from across the business. It says interviewers look at your values as well as your skills, asking whether you take ownership and are adaptable, collaborative and driven. For engineering roles, candidates commonly report coding and system design interviews, often in a shared online editor.
rounds: Recruiter call by video or phone
Interview with one or two team members (for engineers, often a technical or coding interview)
Final round with several people from across the business: technical depth, system design for experienced roles, and values
Decision and feedback from the recruiter
looks_for: Ownership and pride in what you deliver
The thinking behind your results, not just the results

questions.text: Tell me about a piece of work you're proud of. What was your part, and what did it achieve?
covers: The work and why it mattered
Your own part, with the decisions you made
The result, measured if you can

questions.text: Tell me about a time plans changed suddenly. How did you adapt?
covers: What changed and why
How you re-planned and kept others informed
What you delivered and what you learned

questions.text: Tell me about a time you worked closely with people in other disciplines, such as design or data, to ship something.
covers: Who was involved and what each person cared about
A disagreement or trade-off and how you settled it
What shipped and how the collaboration improved it

questions.text: Tell me about a goal you kept pushing towards even when it got hard.
covers: The goal and why it mattered to you
The hardest point and what kept you going
The outcome and what you'd do differently

questions.text: Tell me about a time you tried a new approach that didn't work out. What did you learn?
covers: Why you tried it and what you expected
How you found out it wasn't working
What you kept, what you dropped and what you'd try next

questions.text: How would you design a feature that builds a personalised playlist for each listener every week?
covers: Signals: listening history, skips, saves, similar listeners
Generating playlists in batch, storing them and serving them quickly
Balancing familiar and new music, and measuring success

questions.text: How would you make a song start playing quickly, even on a weak mobile connection?
covers: Content delivery networks and choosing bitrate to match the connection
Buffering or pre-fetching the start of likely next tracks
Caching on the device and measuring time to first play

questions.text: How would you test whether a new home screen layout makes people listen more?
covers: A clear main metric, such as listening time, plus guardrails
An A/B test with a fair split and enough time to settle
Checking effects on different listeners, not only the average

questions.text: Explain the trade-offs of splitting a large app into many small services owned by different teams.
covers: Gains: teams ship independently, services scale separately
Costs: network calls, harder debugging, data spread across services
What helps: clear ownership, good APIs, shared tooling and monitoring

questions.text: Play counts for new releases look too low on an artist dashboard. How would you work out whether the data or the product is wrong?
covers: Comparing the dashboard with the raw data for one release
Checking pipeline delays, filters and counting rules
Telling affected users and fixing the cause

questions.text: Walk me through a system or project you know well: the design, what broke and what you learned.
covers: The goal and a short picture of the design
A failure and how it was handled
What you'd design differently now

questions.text: Why Spotify? How do you use it, and what would you change?
covers: A real habit with the product, as a listener or creator
One specific change and who it would help
Why this team and role in particular

questions.text: What do you want to learn here, and how does this role fit where you're heading?
covers: One or two specific things you want to learn
How the role builds them
What you'll bring in return

tips: Spotify says it tells you who your interviewers are at each stage; look at their teams so your questions fit.
Make the things Spotify asks about easy to hear: shared values, ownership, adaptability, collaboration and drive. Prepare a story for each.
Explain the thinking behind your results, not just the results; Spotify says it wants to understand how you got there.
Technical interviews may use shared tools such as CoderPad; practise coding and explaining in a plain online editor.
